source_span: higher commodity inflation is now pulling the front end with it as the market prices a greater chance the Fed actually responds... Not a great backdrop for multiples.
source_chain: Geopolitical escalation (Iran/Hormuz) pushes crude, gas and distillates higher, therefore this is no longer just a long-end/term-premium story: rising commodity inflation pulls the front end up too as the market prices a greater chance the Fed actually responds, therefore a supply shock hurting growth arrives at the same time the Fed is pushed toward tightening, which is 'not a great backdrop for multiples' (compresses equity multiples). Invalidation: if crude/gas/product prices come down, yields can stabilize and risk has a path to recover (provided NFP/CPI cooperate); if energy keeps rising, the Fed reaction function gets dragged with it and sustained upside becomes much harder. Side-note: heating oil and the US 10yr are trading as the same asset, so relief in rates needs relief in energy first.
pulse_chain: Energy (Brent, European nat gas) spikes to multi-year highs alongside bond yields across the US/Germany/UK/Japan and the S&P falls, therefore (per Goldman's equity sales desk, d2) rising fuel costs pull short-dated yields up too because traders price a higher chance the Fed answers energy with a rate hike, therefore a supply shock slows growth at the same moment policy is pushed tighter, which compresses what investors will pay for earnings; heating oil and the US 10-year are trading as the same asset, so relief in rates needs relief in fuel first. Invalidation: if crude/gas/product prices come down, yields can stabilize and risk assets recover provided payrolls and inflation cooperate; if energy keeps climbing, the constructive case does not hold.
why: The pulse reproduces Privorotsky's exact three-step chain (energy spike -> front-end repriced on Fed-hike odds -> supply shock plus tightening compresses multiples), the same 'same asset' heating-oil/10yr claim, and the identical two-sided invalidation (energy down -> stabilization if data cooperates; energy up -> case breaks), correctly attributed to Goldman's sales desk.
